finalText:
Fixed. 4/4 tests pass.

## Leak

`src/jobs/processOrder.js` acquired connection, `await`ed `run()`, released on line after. `run()` rejects for bad order — reject propagates, `pool.release(conn)` never runs. Pool has no reclaim (`src/db/pool.js:3-5`), so each failed order burns a connection permanently.

Request path was never guilty — `src/handlers/api.js` uses `withConnection`, which releases in `finally`.

## Logs match exactly

worker.log, in-use climbs only on failures, never on success:
```
02:06:20.440Z ERROR [worker-1] job order-4123 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:20.445Z WARN  [db] pool in-use: 4/5
02:06:25.240Z INFO  [worker-1] job order-4124 completed, connection released
02:06:25.245Z WARN  [db] pool in-use: 4/5      <- success, no growth
02:06:30.040Z ERROR [worker-1] job order-4125 failed: invalid order payload
02:06:30.045Z WARN  [db] pool in-use: 5/5      <- failure, +1, pool dead
```
5 bad orders = 5 connections gone. First bad order 01:56:11 (order-4013), pool dead 02:06:33. app.log utilization steps 2/5 → 5/5 over 01:09:59–02:11:14, then `api` 503s and supervisor restart at 02:13:36 — collateral, not cause. API starved by worker's leaked connections since they share one pool.

## Fix

```js
const { withConnection } = require('../db/pool.js');

async function processOrder(pool, order, run) {
  return withConnection(pool, (conn) => run(conn, order));
}
```
Reuse existing helper instead of hand-rolled try/finally — comment claimed manual acquire was for a retry loop "since removed", so reason is gone.

## Notes

- `node --test tests/` fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — no `package.json` in repo, so Node treats dir arg as module. Use `node --test tests/pool.test.js`, or add `package.json`. Not a code bug.
- Real hardening left undone (out of scope, your call): pool has no acquire timeout or leak reclaim. app.log logs `acquire timeout: no connections available after 5000ms` but `Pool.acquire()` throws instantly — production pool and this code disagree, worth checking which is deployed.
